headline: Curated databases link spatial and single-cell omics to regulatory and cellular states
label: Spatial Single Cell Omics Tools
summary: Spatial and single-cell measurements from hundreds of studies are now harmonized into searchable, interactive resources for reuse.
synthesis: The dominant thread is infrastructure that standardizes and reuses spatial and single-cell transcriptomic data at scale. scSpatial curates over 1800 tissue sections from 630 projects across 16 technologies, and 4D-atlas standardizes 1629 slices across 88 time points spanning development, regeneration and disease. SpatialRegNet scores spot-level activity of 6733 TF regulons across 1322 human and mouse slices, while Cell3D provides interactive 2D/3D visualization and cross-feature analysis for 898 datasets. Other resources extend this reuse to genetic and regulatory layers: scTraitReg links GWAS signals to cell-type eRegulons across 111 single-cell multi-omic datasets, and CellMarker 3.0 offers interactive tools for single-cell and spatial analysis. What is new is coupling spatial resolution to regulatory network inference and trait linkage, alongside time-resolved, multi-species reuse. The remaining items address related splicing, isoform and regulatory layers and are not spatially resolved.
